Keeping your battery between 20\u0025 and 80\u0025 can significantly extend its lifespan by reducing stress cycles.
Heat is the #1 enemy of batteries. Avoid intensive gaming or direct sunlight while charging.
Cheap chargers can have unstable voltage, which damages battery cells over time.
OLED screens save significant energy when displaying black pixels. Enable system-wide dark mode.
The screen is the largest consumer. Using auto-brightness or manual low levels extends battery life.
Some apps consume energy even when not in use. Review and restrict high-consumption background apps.
Fast charging generates more heat. Use it only when necessary to preserve cell chemistry.
Letting the battery drain completely stresses the chemical cells. Try to charge it before it drops below 15%.
Sub-zero temperatures slow down ion movement, temporarily reducing effective capacity.
System updates often include power optimizations that improve battery performance.
GPS is a major battery drain. Disable it for apps that don\'t strictly need it.
In areas with poor coverage, your phone increases power to stay connected. Use Airplane Mode.
Connecting to Wi-Fi uses less energy than using 4G/5G mobile data.
Vibration motors consume more energy than ringtones. Disable haptics to save power.
Never leave your device on the car dashboard. Intense heat permanently damages battery capacity.
Gaming or video editing while charging generates excessive heat, accelerating battery wear.
Every notification wakes up the screen and processor. Limit them to the essentials.
High refresh rates (120Hz) are smooth but drain more battery. Use Adaptive mode if available.
Small top–ups throughout the day are better than one long overnight 0–100\u0025 charge.
Reducing the frequency of mail and cloud sync can save a surprising amount of daily energy.
